messages:
luis (customer): Hey team — seeing SSE/chat streaming cut out after ~40-50s of idle. Client reconnects but first chunk is truncated (partial JSON), then subsequent chunks resume. Happens through Cloudflare -> ALB -> nginx -> app. Happens reliably after ~45s idle.

jordan (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (curl/headers) and any server logs when it truncates?

luis (customer): repro: `curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://chat.example.com/stream?session=abc"`
response shows initial `data: {..` then a truncated line and connection close. no 5xx, client sees TCP FIN. logs show no app error, just EOF on connection.

anna (eng-runtime): Two quick suspects: 1) proxy/LB idle timeout closing during app inactivity, 2) proxy buffering or HTTP/2 -> upstream mismatch (h2 multiplexing but upstream expects 1.1 chunked SSE). Cloudflare/ALB + nginx combos often buffer or half-close.

kevin (sre): ALB default idle timeout is 60s; Cloudflare edge to origin timeout is 100s but can do weird half-close on keepalives. Also check NLB vs ALB path — NLB will pass through but ALB may buffer/close when it thinks no activity.

marina (eng-platform): Quick mitigation we recommend: emit a heartbeat SSE comment every 15s from the app (e.g. `: heartbeat\n\n`) and ensure upstream uses `proxy_buffering off` and HTTP/1.1 chunked to origin. Example nginx snippet we use:```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
proxy_cache off;
```
That prevents nginx from coalescing chunks.

luis (customer): trying heartbeat now. curious — any change needed for http2 on ALB/Cloudflare? we are using ALPN h2 between CF and ALB.

anna (eng-runtime): If CF->ALB is h2, ALB->nginx might be http1.1. Multiplexing/h2 windowing can delay frames; some proxies coalesce small SSE events into larger TCP writes after an idle window. Either disable http2 to origin or send periodic non-empty bytes (heartbeat) so buffers flush. Also set `proxy_send_timeout`/`keepalive_timeout` higher.

kevin (sre): Repro tip: run two tests — (A) curl directly to app origin bypassing ALB/nginx (port-forward) and (B) curl through the whole stack. If (A) is stable and (B) fails, it's definitely LB/proxy. Also `tcpdump` shows FIN from ALB side in previous cases.

jordan (support): Thanks — Luis, can you paste `curl -v` output (client side) and the nginx access/err log lines around the abort? if you want we can also schedule a quick call to run tcpdumps.

luis (customer): pasted logs:
```
> GET /stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1
> Host: chat.example.com
> Accept: text/event-stream
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< content-type: text/event-stream
data: {"delta":"hello"}
data: {"delta":" wor

[connection reset by peer]
```
nginx access: `200 - - "GET /stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1"`
nginx error: `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while reading upstream`

marina (eng-platform): That `recv() failed (104)` usually indicates the upstream or ALB closed. Try increasing ALB idle timeout to 300s and disable proxy buffering in nginx. Also add `sendfile off; tcp_nopush off;` in nginx for streaming.

anna (eng-runtime): Also note: if your app uses keepalive but doesn't write for ~45s, some middleboxes will still consider the connection idle. Heartbeat is the fastest fix. We'll add a small library patch to emit `:\n` every 20s by default for streaming endpoints.

kevin (sre): Longer term: Platform tickets to audit Cloudflare page rules and ALB config for streaming paths, and prefer NLB + http1.1 passthrough for SSE-heavy routes. I'll open a ticket to test NLB pass-through behavior for SSE.

jordan (support): Action items: 1) Luis to deploy heartbeat change (15-20s) + set nginx `proxy_buffering off` and `proxy_http_version 1.1`. 2) Kevin to open infra ticket to evaluate ALB vs NLB for streaming. 3) Anna to prepare a small KB snippet with curl repro and nginx + app heartbeat examples.

luis (customer): deployed heartbeat + nginx changes — seems stable in our staging tests, no truncation after long idle. thanks! :tada:

jordan (support): Great — closing this thread, will follow up with infra ticket ID when Kevin posts it. If it recurs, we can do tcpdump/pcap capture with the team. :thumbsup:
